messages:
leo: quick ping 1 — the vanilla ESM quickstart app is hitting TS errors on Vercel Edge preview. Error: 'Type 'RequestInit' is not assignable to type 'Request'' and a bunch of overload mismatches for our `client.responses.create<T>` helper. anyone run into this?

anu: yep. common root cause: the d.ts the app picks up is the CJS one (node-style Request types) while Edge runtime expects DOM Request. package.json exports + types field can cause that.

frank: can you paste the exact call site? overload problems usually mean generic inference failed and TS selected a non-generic overload. that + lib mismatch equals chaos.

leo: call site: `const r = await client.responses.create<MyShape>({ input, stream: false })` inside an edge function. TSC complains about `input` and the call resolution. build uses tsconfig with `module: "ESNext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.

rachel: one more variable: some of our generated d.ts reference `globalThis.Request` vs `import('node-fetch').Request`. If consumer tsconfig includes "dom" lib the types align; otherwise they don't. Edge needs DOM libs.

anu: short fixes: (1) point sample package.json "types" to the ESM bundle (dist/esm/index.d.ts) so resolver doesn't pick cjs, (2) add recommended tsconfig snippet to quickstart that includes lib DOM, (3) add `skipLibCheck: true` in examples as a temporary mitigation.

frank: typing fix idea: we currently ship a pair of overloads:
```ts
export function create<T extends Base = Base>(opts: CreateOptions<T>): Promise<T>
export function create(opts: CreateOptions): Promise<Base>
```
If `opts` has fields typed as `unknown` (we used that to force runtime checks), TS can't infer T and falls back to second overload. Consider collapsing into one signature using conditional types or make the generic inferable via a discriminant: `create<T = Base>(opts: CreateOptions<T> & { _type?: T }): Promise<T>`. Ugly but helps inference.

leo: could we instead provide a tiny helper wrapper in the top-level SDK that maps the internal `unknown`-safe shapes to a friendlier compile-time type (maybe `SDKInput<T> = any` for now) so DX improves while runtime still validates?

rachel: yes, we already do something similar in the Python SDK. For TS we can expose `client.responses.createLoose` with friendlier types and keep strict runtime checks in `client.responses.__internalCreate`. That keeps backward-compat and helps onboarding.

anu: build system note: our bundler was tree-shaking the retry/auth middleware in the ESM entry because no import side-effects were detected. That explains runtime parity issues between npm installs (CJS path had side-effectful require that kept middleware). Quick mitigation: add an explicit side-effect import (e.g., `import './register-default-retries';`) in the ESM entry or mark the module as having side effects in package.json.

frank: long-term: produce a single types bundle (dist/types/index.d.ts) and reference it from both exports. Emit only once during build to avoid duplicate, conflicting d.ts for cjs/esm. Also add a dts-compare test that runs `tsc` in a sample edge project.

leo: can someone scope a tiny PR: (A) change sample package.json types to dist/esm/index.d.ts, (B) add quickstart docs to recommend tsconfig for Edge (`{"module":"ESNext","moduleResolution":"bundler","lib":["DOM","ES2021"],"skipLibCheck":true}`), and (C) add a DTS smoke test running against the quickstart on our edge matrix? I'll triage.

frank: I'll own (A) + DTS test. I'll also add a small DTS unit that asserts `client.responses.create<MyType>` resolves to `MyType` in a minimal sample so we catch regressions.

rachel: I'll prototype the `createLoose` wrapper and open a RFC PR for the typing changes (collapse overloads vs helper wrapper). I'll include before/after `.d.ts` snippets and a user-facing note.

anu: I'll add E2E matrix entry to run the sample app on edge ESM with the auth+retry smoke path. The CI should fail if retries are not invoked (we can assert via a test double).

ci-bot: queued job for branch frank/esm-dts-pin (job 5932) - running dts smoke job :gear:

leo: thank you all 1. this is blocking a couple of customer trials so high priority. once PRs land let's run the customer repro and close loop. also we should add a blurb in onboarding "Known ESM/Edge TS pitfalls" with recommended tsconfig and package.json types guidance.

frank: agreed. adding that to the PR description. i'll also bump the sample app's devDependencies to the same TS major we run internally to reduce mismatch surprises.

rachel: FYI — I found one place where we used `unknown` deeply inside `ResponseBody` types. swapping that pocket to `Record<string, any>` inside the SDK entry dramatically improved inference in the sample without loosening runtime checks (we still validate at runtime). I'll add the test results to the RFC PR.

leo: perfect. keep this thread posted and ping me if you need reviewers. :thumbsup:
